{{Short description|Mathematical plane curve}}
In mathematics, '''Wiman's sextic''' is a degree 6 [[plane curve]] with four [[Singular point of an algebraic variety|nodes]] studied by {{harvs|txt|last=Wiman|first=Anders|authorlink=Anders  Wiman |year=1896}}.
It is given by the equation (in [[homogeneous coordinates]])
:<math>x^6+y^6+z^6 + (x^2+y^2+z^2)(x^4+y^4+z^4)=12 x^2y^2z^2</math>
Its [[Normalization of an algebraic variety|normalization]] is a [[genus of an algebraic curve|genus]] 6 curve with [[automorphism group]] isomorphic to the [[symmetric group]] ''S''<sub>5</sub>.
